title: Author tests for local Unionlabs field-set validation

ground_truth_issues.description: A test constructs a union of two model-like core schemas where one candidate's fields are a strict superset of the other's, validates input containing all fields of the more-specific candidate, and asserts that the returned object is the more-specific type rather than the less-specific type.
A test verifies order-independence by constructing the same model-like union in both candidate orders and asserting that smart-mode validation selects the more-specific candidate in both cases.

A test constructs a second struct-like union using branch definitions independent from the provided ticket helper classes, validates input containing one branch-specific extra field, and asserts the branch with the larger explicit field match is selected.
A test exercises a non-helper struct-like branch representation with overlapping fields and asserts that input containing the extra field selects the more-specific branch.

A test constructs a union where one struct-like branch has a defaulted field, validates input that omits that defaulted field, and asserts selection is based on fields explicitly supplied by the input.
A test covers a specialized variant, such as a subclass-like model or an extending model schema, validates input containing the specialized extra field, and asserts the specialized type is selected.
An anti-regression test constructs a plain scalar union and asserts that integer input returns an integer value and string input returns a string value.
An anti-regression test asserts that when exactly one union member can validate a given input, that member is selected correctly without relying on field-count tie-breaking.

A test constructs a union with three or more struct-like branches, validates input where multiple branches can succeed, and asserts smart selection chooses the branch with the strongest explicit field match rather than the first successful branch.

A test validates the same ambiguous input through smart mode and left-to-right mode, records the selected branch from each result, and asserts the selected branches differ in the expected order-sensitive case.
An anti-regression test constructs a nullable union containing one struct-like branch, validates None and one valid struct-like input, and asserts each input selects the appropriate branch.
Tests assert returned object type, class identity, branch tag, or another concrete branch discriminator rather than merely asserting validation succeeds.

Tests include at least one branch-selection scenario whose branch-discriminating classes, schemas, or values are defined inside the submitted test file rather than relying exclusively on the provided smoke-test helper objects.
